what_they_do: Kinth turns constraint sheets, sketches, engineering drawings, and performance requirements into editable, CAD-native parametric models, rather than the mesh-based outputs most AI design tools produce. It replaces the manual, repetitive CAD work engineers do to translate a spec into a usable model: building geometry by hand, running it through simulation, checking it against manufacturability rules, and revising it over and over. Kinth generates multiple CAD-ready design concepts in parallel from the same requirements, runs simulation-informed iteration against those constraints, and flags design-for-manufacturing issues, so engineers can compare tradeoffs earlier and spend less time on early-stage prototyping and revision cycles.
vertical: AI-native parametric CAD / engineering design software for hardware, construction, robotics, manufacturing, and aerospace teams
theme_fit_rationale: Kinth's wedge is ingesting unstructured inputs (constraint sheets, sketches, freehand drawings) that legacy CAD tools can't read, and using that to automatically produce structured, manufacturable parametric models, then compounding into downstream simulation and DFM automation as more designs pass through the system (Theme 5). Secondarily, by generating CAD-native, manufacturable geometry that plugs into existing workflows and runs DFM checks, it functions as a bridge connecting design tools to manufacturing, one of the explicit use cases under the hardware supply chain theme (Theme 7).
